name: a line comment ends at a lone carriage return
about: Synthetic: written by hand for kangzj/lantern-tv#657. Gson 2.14.0 ends a comment at \r as well as \n.

name: a trailing comma in an object or an array is dropped, where Gson refuses one or reads a null
about: Synthetic: written by hand for kangzj/lantern-tv#657. More lenient than FongMi on purpose: Gson 2.14.0 refuses the document for the object's comma, and reads the array's as an extra null site.

name: a comment after the document is skipped, where Gson refuses it
about: Synthetic: written by hand for kangzj/lantern-tv#657. More lenient than FongMi on purpose: Gson 2.14.0 refuses any comment after the top-level value.

name: a key missing its opening quote is refused, where Gson reads it with the quote in the key
about: Synthetic: written by hand for kangzj/lantern-tv#657. Stricter than FongMi on purpose: Gson 2.14.0 reads an unquoted key named ext", so the site loses its ext. xn--z7x900a.net (39 sites) is written this way.

name: a stray quote after a value is refused, where Gson reads it into the value
about: Synthetic: written by hand for kangzj/lantern-tv#657. Stricter than FongMi on purpose: Gson 2.14.0 reads searchable as the string 0". tv.nxog.top 111.php (114 sites) is written this way.

name: an escape JSON does not have is refused, as Gson refuses it
about: Synthetic: written by hand for kangzj/lantern-tv#657. Gson 2.14.0 refuses \a and \x41.

name: a comma before a # comment and then the close is a trailing comma
about: Synthetic: written by hand for kangzj/lantern-tv#657. The # twin of the // case above: the comma is dropped as that one is.

about: Synthetic: written by hand for kangzj/lantern-tv#595. m3u8.apiyhzy.com is written this way and answers XML (measured 2026-09-24); FongMi reads type alone and shows it empty.

name: a type 1 entry whose query names at/xml is read as XML
about: Synthetic: written by hand for kangzj/lantern-tv#595. anltv and ah121 are written this way.

name: a type 0 entry whose address names at/json is read as JSON
about: Synthetic: written by hand for kangzj/lantern-tv#595. The same rule the other way round, so it reads as one sentence.

name: a plain address is read by its type
about: Synthetic: written by hand for kangzj/lantern-tv#595. What must not change.

name: at/xml straight after an = or inside a word names nothing
about: Synthetic: written by hand for kangzj/lantern-tv#595. The dialect is named only after a `/`, `?` or `&`, and ends where the item does.

name: a type-50 entry keeps the type it names, whatever its address says
about: Synthetic: written by hand for kangzj/lantern-tv#595. A Yonto entry names its type outright; only a numbered entry is typed by guesswork.

name: only the path and query name a dialect, and they end where the item does
about: Synthetic: written by hand for kangzj/lantern-tv#595, from its review. A fragment and a host are not what the server is asked for, and a trailing U+0085, which Java's `$` would have taken for the end, is not the end of an item.

name: an address wrapped in a query names the dialect, and the first one named wins
about: Synthetic: written by hand for kangzj/lantern-tv#595, from its second review. A proxy passing the real address in a query value is asking the wrapped server, so its `at/xml` counts, and an address naming both dialects is read in the one it names first, on a type 0 so that neither the last nor the type could produce the answer.

name: a type-50 xptv-js entry's program is its config's ext
about: Synthetic: written by hand for kangzj/lantern-tv#698. On a type-50 entry `ext` is the Yonto object, so the program's address is `ext.config.ext`, and one with none is skipped for its address. A numbered type 3 still takes `ext` as the program and `api` as its class.
